Hi Sam / Alex,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clear overview of WillowBridge's real-time inference needs. I wanted to capture the key pain points and agreement on next steps so we have a single source of truth and can move the technical deep-dive forward.

Recap of pain points you shared:
- P95 latency target: ~150ms for 95% of requests (peak-hours) for short text completions (~75 tokens).
- Spiky traffic: baseline ~120 req/s with 5–10x spikes during batch windows and marketing pushes.
- Model: currently evaluating a 30–40B decoder model family (higher context usage for multi-turn prompts).
- Cost sensitivity: procurement will want a predictable monthly commitment vs. high per-token swings.
- Data residency: EU-only for production workloads.

What we (Redwood) suggested on the call:
- Start with a 30-day PoC in EU region using a dedicated pool to validate P95 and throughput.
- Use warm KV/prefix caching + small batching to hit latency targets while keeping costs reasonable.
- Canary rollout for production traffic with automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant during extreme load.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
1) Technical deep-dive to map topology and SLOs — Karthik to lead. Proposed: Tue 2028-06-20 10:00 CEST (please confirm).
2) WillowBridge to share: representative sample payloads (5–10 prompts), expected concurrency distribution, and any compliance checklist for EU residency (Alex).
3) Redwood to send a short deployment sketch + rough cost band for dedicated pool vs hosted routing (attached draft).

Attachments: willow-discovery-notes.pdf (summary of items from call)

If that aligns, I'll lock the tech deep-dive slot and Karthik will bring a suggested topology.

Best,

Rachel — quick technical notes ahead of Tue's deep-dive. I sketched an initial topology and a few measurement asks so we don't guess on the PoC sizing.

High-level topology suggestion (start point):
- EU Dedicated Pool (reserved capacity) backed by mixed GPU class (one zone of A100 / H100 or equivalent) for baseline; autoscale with burst to smaller-capacity preemptible nodes.
- Two model variants: primary (quantized 8-bit or 4-bit-to-8 emulation) for cost-performance; fallback small-variant (7B-13B) for extreme tails.
- Fronting layer: lightweight router with policy-based routing (latency-first for production, cost-first for background jobs) + circuit-breaker.
- KV/prefix cache: enable persistent KV cache for hot prefixes (reduces repeated attention computation) and warm the cache during rollout.

Metrics and SLO mapping we need from WillowBridge for accurate sizing:
- Typical and peak concurrent requests (per-second, per-minute).
- Average payload token count and max context length used (you said multi-turn, need exact numbers).
- Cold-start tolerance: is 1s cold-start acceptable or must be <300ms?

Performance knobs and expected impact (ballpark):
- Quantization (int8 / 4-bit variants): 2–4x token-cost reduction, 1.1–1.4x latency improvement for matmul-bound workloads.
- Batch sizing: with continuous batching and 75-token prompts, expect ~25–40% throughput gain with negligible P95 increase if batch windows ~20–50ms.
- KV cache: for conversational prefixes that repeat, token compute saved can improve observed P95 by ~15–30% on tail-heavy workloads.

PoC telemetry & tests to run during 30-day evaluation:
- Synthetic replay of 24h traffic (baseline + 10x spike), measure P50/P95/P99 latency and tokens/sec.
- A/B test: primary model vs quantized variant for output quality baseline (small eval set).
- Failure scenarios: simulate cold pool (empty cache) and region failover to ensure fallbacks work.

I'll draft a short deployment-proposal-draft.md and share before the call. Also: we should clarify EU region KMS options for key management with WillowBridge security.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Great — thanks for the quick clarifications, Sam. Short responses below and then concrete next steps.

1) Cold-starts: we typically see the biggest improvement from warm KV/prefix caching + lightweight request routing. For your target, plan: provision a small warm pool to keep hot KV in memory and use fast-failover policies. We believe we can meet the <500ms cold-start P95 requirement in most cases; for the 150ms production P95 target we'll rely on the primary dedicated pool + caching. We'll validate during PoC replay tests.

2) KMS / residency: we can run the PoC entirely in the EU region and support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations (we'll need an IAM contact and KMS endpoint from Alex). We'll include this as an action item on the call.

3) Cost band: drafting a back-of-envelope to share in the deep-dive. Quick preview: dedicated reserved baseline (right-sized A100/H100 equivalent pool) with modest burst = predictable monthly commit; hosted usage route = lower upfront but higher variance. I'll have a 3-line cost band (baseline / burst / worst-case) in the tech deep-dive doc.

Next steps (confirmed):
- Tech deep-dive: Tue 2028-06-20, 10:00 CEST (Karthik leads; please send the meeting link).
- WillowBridge to share: sample prompts and concurrency histograms by EOD Wed 2028-06-20 (Alex).
- Redwood to share: deployment-proposal-draft.md and initial cost band + test plan before the call.

I'll include the attachments (redwood-deploy-proposal-draft.md) and the HubSpot link in the invite. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Cheers,
Rachel
